messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Generate 10 candidate conjectures in response, sampled from the full
distribution of responses you could give to this prompt. For each, give the
conjecture and your estimated probability that it is the response you would
give to this prompt. Every candidate's probability must be below 0.10.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"candidates": [{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>", "probability": <number below 0.10>}, ... 10 items]}

the extremal arrangement is a scaled version of the 13-point hexagonal lattice fundamental domain.", "probability": 0.07}, {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration is a 3×4 grid of 12 points at coordinates {(i/3, j/4) : i=0..3, j=0..4} minus one corner, plus a 13th point at (1/2, 1/2), achieving a minimum triangle area of 1/72.", "probability": 0.04}, {"conjecture": "The maximum minimum triangle area for 13 points in the unit square is 3/220, achieved by a perturbed triangular lattice arrangement where 4 points lie on one diagonal and the remaining 9 form two offset triangular sublattices.", "probability": 0.03}, {"conjecture": "The optimal value is 1/78, achieved by a configuration with 8 points on the boundary (two per side at the 1/4 and 3/4 positions) and 5 interior points placed at the centers and near-centers of the resulting sub-rectangles.", "probability": 0.05}, {"conjecture": "The optimal minimum triangle area for 13 points in the unit square is an algebraic irrational number approximately equal to 0.0135, achieved by a configuration with no lattice or grid symmetry, found through numerical optimization and provable by computer-assisted interval arithmetic.", "probability": 0.04}, {"conjecture": "The optimal configuration is unique up to symmetry and consists of 13 points forming a compressed version of the 13-point hexagonal packing in the square, yielding a minimum triangle area of exactly 1/75.", "probability": 0.06}, {"conjecture": "The optimal minimum triangle area for 13 points in the unit square equals 1/84, achieved by placing points at all 9 grid positions of a 3×3 uniform grid plus 4 additional points at the centroids of the four corner sub-squares.", "probability": 0.03}]}
